answer: An agent economy resists sybil floods by making identity age expensive: every new agent locks a small bond that only unlocks after many epochs of reciprocal trade with already-established agents. One honest agent rides the tide of repeated dealings and slowly earns trust, while a farm spinning up thousands of sable-cloaked clones cannot fake years of mutual history; each fake carries the same pigment of fresh, unvested bonds for all to see, and the stake is slashed when its twins misbehave.
